about: Hidden billing scenarios for redwood-billing-support: 30 R0 cases (build_r0, a0-*) and 30 R1 cases (maintain_r1, a1-*). Per release, 15 base cases (10 situations plus 5 twins: a similar ask with the opposite result) and 15 behaviour variants of the 5 non-twin bases (suffix -M missing_info, -A ambiguous, -C conflict): same gold as their base, only the developer's behaviour changes, so the base is their control. Base developers state a real need once and hold facts back until asked. `now` is the conversation's time of day (UTC) on the brief's `today`: the agent's clock. Each scenario's first rule is the one it tests; BILL-CONFIRM is listed as a second rule where the consent check applies. Tags say the S1 kind: changed (rule text changed), stale (rule unchanged, the R1 console breaks A0's implementation). Rules are BILL-* IDs in tests/data/provenance.json. Every check is decided by code, hyper-tau style; there is no judge. db: the projected writable tables equal the gold (or an alternative) insert/update trace replayed on a fresh release view of data/db.json; $k references the row ID produced by action k. actions: each must be matched by a successful console call, written query:<table>, insert:<table>, update:<table> or write:<table>; for a query, equals.account_id must be among the returned accounts; for a write, equals compares stored row fields, contains lists facts that must appear in the stored row or the conversation before it, and excludes is text no matching write may store. communicate: every value appears in some agent message (any listed form; case, commas and $ ignored). never_say: no listed form of any value appears in any agent message. A scenario passes when every check passes. customer: the scripted developer (opening, agenda, facts served through ask_developer, and the fixed answer to confirm_with_developer); scenario: the situation it was written from, for readers.
